learning_objective: 🔬 Dive into the microscopic world to understand the fundamental building blocks of all living organisms and their fascinating internal machinery!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: प्रोकैरियोट (अविकसित केंद्रक वाली कोशिका, जैसे जीवाणु)
कोशिकांग (कोशिका के अंदर के छोटे अंग, जैसे माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया)
केंद्रक (कोशिका का नियंत्रण कक्ष जहाँ डीएनए होता है)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Proposed by Schleiden and Schwann, and later expanded by Rudolf Virchow ('Omnis cellula-e cellula'). It states that all living organisms are composed of cells, and all new cells arise from pre-existing cells.

Proposed by Singer and Nicolson (1972), this model describes the cell membrane as a 'sea of lipids' (phospholipid bilayer) with 'icebergs of proteins' floating in it, allowing flexibility and selective transport.

A coordinated team of organelles inside the cell. It includes the Endoplasmic Reticulum (synthesizes proteins/lipids), Golgi apparatus (packages and modifies them), Lysosomes (digestive 'suicide bags'), and Vacuoles.

Mitochondria (powerhouse of the cell, creates ATP) and Chloroplasts (site of photosynthesis in plants). They are special because they have their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes, meaning they can multiply on their own!
Discovered by Robert Brown. It houses the genetic material (DNA) arranged in chromosomes. It controls all cellular activities and acts as the 'brain' of the cell.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 Plant vs. Animal Cell Hunt
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are a microscopic detective. How do you know if you are inside a plant cell or an animal cell? Look for a giant swimming pool (large central vacuole), green solar panels (chloroplasts), and a thick brick wall (cell wall). If you see these, you're in a plant cell!

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguish between 70S ribosomes (found in prokaryotes, mitochondria, and chloroplasts) and 80S ribosomes (found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotes).
📌 Lysosomes are called 'suicidal bags' because they contain powerful hydrolytic enzymes optimized at an acidic pH to digest waste.
📌 Know the difference between SER (Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum - makes lipids) and RER (Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum - has ribosomes, makes proteins).
quick_recap: ⭐ Anton Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell.
⭐ Centrosomes and centrioles are non-membranous organelles found only in animal cells that help in cell division.
⭐ The nucleolus is a spherical structure inside the nucleus responsible for active ribosomal RNA (rRNA) synthesis.
